description: Search the directory of developer services (hosting, databases, auth, email, SMS, payments, analytics, monitoring, LLM APIs, vector databases, search, CMS and more): what each provider sells, its free tier, its lowest paid price, caveats and the pricing page it came from. Wider than the cost engine: use it to find options or check a provider the other tools don't price. Entries marked candidate have no prices yet. A provider can carry availability (acquired, shutting_down) and an admin_note: say so when you mention it. Services that shut down are left out unless include_closed is true. Example: {"query":"postgres","category":"database"}.

category.description: Directory category id, e.g. database, email, sms, llm, vector_db. Every result lists the categories with counts.

in_cost_engine.description: true: only providers estimate_cost and plan_stack can price.

include_closed.description: true: include services that have shut down (left out by default; an exact id always finds one).

query.description: Words to match, e.g. "sms", "vector", "merchant of record", "Supabase", or a company such as "Amazon" for all its services.

status.description: researched: prices read from the pricing page. candidate: listed without prices.

name: search_directory

assumptions.description: Usage and pricing assumptions behind the numbers.

caveats.description: Show to the user word for word.

completeness.description: On plan and project results: complete, complete_with_assumptions, incomplete or needs_clarification, with the reasons. Say plainly when it is not complete.

data.description: The tool result. Its shape depends on the tool.

disclosures.description: Always includes the neutrality note: no vendor pays for a place in the answer. Link its url when you mention how Kong Reviews is paid.

project.description: On results about a saved project: its id and the context version the answer was computed on. Pass both back in follow-up calls.

title: Search the service directory
